newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 30.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:

- A U.S. federal grand jury is investigating whether aircraft maker McDonnell Douglas Corp or the Chinese government knowingly violated U.S. export-import laws two years ago in a $1.6 billion order for 40 airplanes.
- French luxury goods conglomerate LVMH Moet Hennessy-Louis Vuitton has signed an agreement to buy a controlling interest in DFS Group Ltd worth $2.47 billion.
- Saks Fifth Avenue of the holding company Saks Holdings Inc is arranging plans to try to buy bankrupt luxury retailer Barneys Inc.
- U.S. government reaffirmed a decision preventing Tele-Communications Inc from transmitting a direct-broadcasting satellite service to U.S. homes from a Canadian-owned satellite.
- News Corp Ltd promoted Peter Chermin, chairman of the 20th Century Fox unit, to the new position of president of News Corp.
- America Online Inc announced a new pricing setup, a new management organization, a new top manager and a new accounting policy.
- Compaq Computer Corp introduced its first line of work stations.
- Microsoft Corp said Patty Stonesifer is to resign as senior vice president of the company's interactive media division.
- Fashion design company Donna Karan International Inc saw it stock price fall 17 percent on the New York Stock Exchange after releasing poor quarterly results.
- Supplies of heating oil and diesel fuel rose sharply last week.
- U.S. government said the growth of workers' wages and benefits slowed down during the third quarter.
